description: The Modified Discrete Cosine Transform (MDCT) decomposed. MDCT is the canonical perceptual-audio transform: DCT-IV applied to overlapping blocks with TDAC (Time-Domain Aliasing Cancellation) windowing. Perfect reconstruction at 50% overlap means no doubled-bitrate cost despite the overlap. Used by MP3 (576-pt hybrid), AAC (1024/128-pt), Vorbis, Opus's CELT mode.

sub_mechanisms.name: dct_iv_basis
sub_mechanisms.definition: MDCT is built on the Type-IV DCT: basis cos((2k+1)(2n+1)π/(4N)). Frequency-domain output of length N from time-domain input of length 2N (overlapping).
sub_mechanisms.why: DCT-IV has the property that its forward + inverse on overlapping windows produces aliasing in the time-domain output that exactly CANCELS across adjacent windows when summed. This is the mathematical underpinning of TDAC.

sub_mechanisms.name: fifty_percent_overlap
sub_mechanisms.definition: Successive MDCT blocks overlap by 50% — input window of length 2N produces output of length N; each input sample is part of TWO consecutive blocks.
sub_mechanisms.why: Without overlap, transform-boundary discontinuities cause coding artifacts. 50% overlap with proper windowing smooths the transitions. TDAC's perfect-reconstruction property only holds at exactly 50% overlap with sine-style windows.

sub_mechanisms.name: time_domain_aliasing_cancellation
sub_mechanisms.definition: TDAC: aliasing introduced by forward MDCT of each overlapped window exactly cancels when adjacent windows' inverse-MDCT outputs are overlap-added. The output is the input, sample-perfect.
sub_mechanisms.why: The mathematical magic that makes MDCT work for audio. Naively, downsampling by 2 (overlap) + transform would alias; TDAC's window+transform structure ensures the aliasing terms have opposite signs in adjacent windows and cancel exactly.

sub_mechanisms.name: sine_window
sub_mechanisms.definition: Standard MDCT window: w(n) = sin(π(n+0.5)/2N). Satisfies the Princen-Bradley condition: w(n)² + w(n+N)² = 1, required for perfect reconstruction.
sub_mechanisms.why: The simplest window satisfying TDAC. Smooth transitions reduce spectral leakage at block boundaries. Used by Vorbis, Opus CELT, and AAC's main window type.

sub_mechanisms.name: kaiser_bessel_window
sub_mechanisms.definition: AAC's alternative window: a Kaiser-Bessel-derived window with steeper transition than sine. Different perceptual trade-offs.
sub_mechanisms.why: Steeper transition → less spectral leakage but more pre/post-echo. AAC's KBD window is preferred for some content types; sine window for others. Per-block choice gives encoders content-adaptive flexibility.

sub_mechanisms.name: long_block_1024
sub_mechanisms.definition: AAC long block: 2048 input samples → 1024 output coefficients. Provides fine frequency resolution.
sub_mechanisms.why: Steady-state signals (sustained tones, instrumental music) benefit from fine frequency resolution. Long blocks have better spectral discrimination but spread quantisation noise across ~25 ms of time, vulnerable to pre-echo on transients.

sub_mechanisms.name: short_block_128
sub_mechanisms.definition: AAC short block: 256 input samples → 128 output coefficients. Used as a sequence of 8 short blocks within one 'short-block frame' to maintain bitstream structure.
sub_mechanisms.why: Transient signals (drums, percussion) need short blocks to limit pre-echo to ~3 ms. The 8-block grouping keeps the bitstream's frame structure consistent. Encoder switches based on transient detection.

sub_mechanisms.name: start_stop_windows
sub_mechanisms.definition: Transitional windows used when switching between long and short blocks. Half-long-shape, half-short-shape windows preserve TDAC across the size change.
sub_mechanisms.why: Direct long→short transitions would break TDAC. Start/stop windows are designed to be perfect-reconstruction-compatible with both adjacent block types. Cost: a small encoding latency to determine when to switch.

sub_mechanisms.name: mp3_hybrid_filterbank
sub_mechanisms.definition: MP3 first applies a 32-band polyphase filterbank, then an MDCT (18-pt long or 6-pt short) within each subband. 32 × 18 = 576 final coefficients per frame.
sub_mechanisms.why: MP3 inherited the polyphase from MPEG-1 Layer I/II, added MDCT for finer resolution within each subband. The two-stage approach is computationally heavier than pure MDCT but provides the band-aligned structure MP3 was designed around.

sub_mechanisms.name: fft_based_implementation
sub_mechanisms.definition: MDCT can be computed via an N-point FFT (via twiddle-factor multiplications) rather than the direct O(N²) DCT-IV matrix multiplication.
sub_mechanisms.why: FFT brings the cost from O(N²) to O(N log N). For N=1024 (AAC long), this is 100x faster. Standard implementation in all production codecs. Decoder-side IMDCT uses the same trick.

sub_mechanisms.name: spectral_envelope_concentration
sub_mechanisms.definition: MDCT concentrates the energy of natural audio signals into a small number of low-frequency coefficients. The high-frequency coefficients are typically much smaller in magnitude.
sub_mechanisms.why: Same insight as DCT for images: audio is mostly low-frequency. The energy concentration lets perceptual coders allocate more bits to low frequencies (where energy is) and fewer to high (where masking is also stronger).

sub_mechanisms.name: imdct_perfect_inverse
sub_mechanisms.definition: The inverse MDCT (IMDCT) outputs the original time-domain signal sample-for-sample, when TDAC and overlap-add are correctly applied.
sub_mechanisms.why: Lossless inverse (in the absence of quantisation) is the foundation of all MDCT-based codecs. Quantisation between MDCT and IMDCT is what introduces loss; the transform itself is information-preserving.

derivation_rules.name: fifty_percent_overlap_required_for_TDAC
if: MDCT uses 50% overlap with TDAC-compatible windows
then: perfect reconstruction is achievable without redundancy
derivation_rules.why: TDAC's mathematical structure requires exactly 50% overlap; lower overlap doesn't cancel aliasing, higher overlap is redundant (sends each sample more than twice). Princen-Bradley condition on windows formalises this.

derivation_rules.name: long_blocks_for_steady_state_short_for_transients
then: short MDCT blocks limit pre-echo to the transient's duration
derivation_rules.why: Quantisation noise is spread across the temporal extent of the transform block. Long blocks spread it across ~25 ms (audible pre-echo before transients); short blocks confine it to ~3 ms (masked by the transient itself).

derivation_rules.name: fft_implementation_amortises_cost
if: MDCT is computed via N-point FFT
then: compute drops from O(N²) to O(N log N)
derivation_rules.why: DCT-IV can be expressed as a complex FFT with pre/post multiplications. Same energy compaction at much lower compute cost. Universal in production codecs.

derivation_rules.name: window_choice_balances_leakage_and_transient_response
if: a codec must choose a transform window
then: sine windows are simplest; KBD windows trade leakage for transient handling
derivation_rules.why: Different windows have different time-frequency localisation. Sine is the smoothest; KBD has sharper transitions. Per-block adaptive choice (AAC) optimises per content; fixed choice (Vorbis sine, Opus sine) is simpler but slightly suboptimal.
